name: Resizable
summary: Keyboard and pointer resizable panels with finite percentage sizes.

useWhen: Letting a user resize adjacent panels
avoidWhen: A fixed divider between regions; use Separator

obligations: Expose each handle as a separator with value bounds.

behavior: Arrow keys and pointer motion resize adjacent panels.
An arrow key moves a handle by keyboardStep percent, and Shift with an arrow key moves it by keyboardLargeStep.

Home and End move a handle to the smallest and largest size its two panels allow. Page Up and Page Down move it by keyboardLargeStep in the same direction as the Up and Down arrows when vertical, or the Left and Right arrows when horizontal, mirrored in right-to-left.
precision sets how many decimal places sizes keep, from 0 to 10.
Sizes are percentages. minSize and maxSize bound each panel, and the sizes of a valid layout always add up to 100.
Direct children alternate Panel, Handle, Panel, with a Panel at each end. Fragments are allowed; other wrapper elements are not.
Panel and Handle ids are unique, start with a letter, and use only letters, digits, underscores, and hyphens.
before and after on each Handle are the ids of the Panels on either side of it.
Each Handle has exactly one non-blank accessible name, from aria-label or aria-labelledby.
minSize and maxSize are numbers from 0 to 100 with minSize at most maxSize, the minimums add up to at most 100, and the maximums to at least 100.
keyboardStep and keyboardLargeStep must be finite numbers greater than 0.
A controlled sizes object has a finite size for every Panel id and no other keys, each within that Panel's bounds, adding up to 100.
An uncontrolled defaultSizes that is missing, or does not add up to 100, is adjusted to a valid layout.
Passing both sizes and defaultSizes is invalid.
An invalid composition or configuration does not throw: the root and its panels are marked data-invalid and every handle is disabled.
onSizesChange runs on every change, and onSizesCommit runs when a pointer gesture that changed the sizes ends normally and after each keyboard change.
Both callbacks receive the sizes and an object with the handle id and the source, pointer or keyboard.

A pointer gesture ends without calling onSizesCommit when it is cancelled, loses pointer capture, the window is resized, or the Resizable becomes disabled or read-only. If it had changed the sizes, onSizesChange runs once more with the sizes from before the gesture, unless they no longer form a valid layout. An uncontrolled Resizable then shows them again, and a controlled parent applies them like any other change. Nothing is reported when the Resizable unmounts, or when a controlled parent shows sizes other than the ones the gesture last proposed, or other than its starting sizes before its first change. In both cases the gesture ends without reporting.
A horizontal Resizable fills the width of its container, and a vertical one fills the height of its container when that container has a height.
accessibility: Each handle is an operable separator with percentage values.
Horizontal layouts expose vertical separators and vertical layouts expose horizontal separators.

requirements.reason: Native colors do not apply to web React.
Native font metrics do not apply to web React.
